# Enabled roles

The effective config runs these pipeline roles: reader, producer, verifier. Any other role does not run for this job.

# Reading rules

- Previous result: a retry or follow-up names each earlier job, how its result is addressed, deliverables, out_of_scope, and each changed file kept or excluded (`check_prior_result_and_scope`).
- Criteria evidence: each criterion rests on a command, Grep or file the verifier can check, not the producer's report (`check_criteria_evidence`).
- Governance files: when the request names one or a deliverable implies it, list it and name it in a criterion, or in out_of_scope (`check_governance_coverage`).
- Code survey: a code or tests reading with a behavior criterion has a `Code survey:` assumption naming crates/ paths (`check_code_survey`).
- Design: an `Existing code:` assumption names crates/ or docs/ paths the job does not create; a criterion reuses or extends them (`check_design_existing_code`).
- Environment: a CI workflow, push, PR, or records-branch or history read needs an `Environment:` assumption: site, read/write permissions, data reached (`check_environment_reach`).
- Terms: define each structural term in the request (ladder, rung, tier, layer) in a `Term ladder: <meaning>` assumption; a quoted mention needs none (`check_defined_terms`).
- Scope limit: a limiting criterion lists CHANGELOG.md or says `the deliverables`; a config deliverable needs `Consumers: <paths>` or `Consumers: none found` (`check_scope_limit`).
- Records measures: changing throughput, keep rule, planning cost, refusal rate or landing time needs a criterion run on real records with an expected range from an independent source (`check_records_measure`).
- Valid reading: class, capability and producer model from closed lists; a decline gives a reason; a capability needs a criterion; valid forecasts (`build_reading`).
- Test placement: put each test where it can import the code; xtask has no library, so use `xtask/tests/` or unit tests in `xtask/src/` (prose only).
- Enabled roles: brief content targets only roles under Enabled roles (prose only).
- Reused field, CLI argument, record key or config key needs `Field meaning:` assumption: quote documented meaning (crates/ or config path:line), why it fits, config: live athena.toml value; or a new field (prose only).
- Behavior: for a loop (drain, queue), protection or rendered output, a criterion names the real path run end to end, its effect (item landed, record written) and a check that fails without it (prose only).

Before you give behavior criteria for a code or tests change, read the code and write one assumption that starts with `Code survey:` and names the crates/ paths you read. # Checkable criteria

Every acceptance criterion must be checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs, never from the producer's report or change description, which the verifier does not see. Write each criterion so its check names a file, a diff line or a command the verifier can run (listed under What the verifier can run when given).

# Rules that judge criteria

Athena applies these rules when it judges the criteria you write. They are not preferences: a criterion that contradicts one cannot be met.

- D43 (verifier rule, `must cite commands that ran (D43)`): a behavior criterion is met only by commands that ran; its evidence must cite them. Name the command the verifier runs or a recorded Athena check. A content criterion names a file or a diff line.
- D63 (verifier rule, `as one whole simple command inside a chained or piped one`): the verifier sees a chained or piped command only as each whole simple command in it, so name each command as its own simple command; part of a command does not count.
- D115 (verifier rule, `Athena ran and recorded it on the same candidate tree and it passed`): a passing check that Athena recorded on the same final tree counts as a command run, so fmt, clippy and test can be named as evidence; a failed record, or a record made on another tree, does not count.
- Append-only logs (docs/decisions.md is append-only; records are append-only): never write a criterion that edits, annotates or removes an existing entry of docs/decisions.md or anything under records/. Add a docs/decision-links.toml link only when the new entry supersedes or amends an earlier one, or the change touches a path listed under [[governs]] there.
- Changelog (CHANGELOG.md; the changelog default applies): it is a default-written deliverable (Athena always adds it to a change reading, and the job must record itself there), so a criterion must not forbid changing it. The Scope limit rule above says how to write a limit that allows it.

The verifier exercises behavior criteria only with these commands, from the repository root, with no environment variables of its own, no other programs, and no writes.
